title: U.S. House · Ohio's 4th District
area: North-central Ohio, including Lima and Mansfield

context.text: The Cook Political Report rates the 4th District R+21, a safely Republican-leaning seat.

candidates.name: Jim Jordan
candidates.ballotNote: Incumbent, unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary

positions.summary: In June 2026 he told The National News Desk that there should be a citizenship requirement, in the context of the SAVE America Act, which would require proof of citizenship to register to vote.
positions.quote: We should have photo ID. We should have a citizenship requirement.

record.text: Chairs the House Committee on the Judiciary and serves on the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

priorities.text: Campaign website calls for government accountability and transparency, including a 'Registered Voter Lobby' and a district think tank, and says full-time work 'deserves economic stability.'
Campaign website calls for healthcare reform, including allowing Medicare to negotiate drug prices and increasing price transparency.
Campaign website calls for getting 'big money out of politics,' including repealing Citizens United, banning members of Congress from trading individual stocks, and supporting term limits.

positions.summary: His campaign website says Congress must reclaim its constitutional authority over war and that he would oppose military action unless absolutely necessary.
positions.quote: Congress must reclaim its constitutional authority over war

positions.summary: His campaign website criticizes school voucher programs as funding for-profit schools at the cost of public education.
positions.quote: School voucher programs are trying to fund for-profit schools at the cost of public education for Ohio’s youth.

statements.quote: Explore both public and private options that reduce costs for every American
statements.context: On his campaign website, under healthcare reform
On his campaign website, listed under legislative goals

candidates.name: Tracey Tackett

priorities.text: Says she is an independent who believes 'solving problems is more important than partisan fighting' and will work with anyone with a good idea.
priorities.quote: I'm an Independent who believes solving problems is more important than partisan fighting.

priorities.text: Says decisions should empower local governments and institutions, and pledges to 'bring resources back home, support first responders, strengthen infrastructure.'
Calls for fiscal responsibility and government transparency, and for supporting agriculture and small businesses.

positions.summary: Her campaign website says the country must end all illegal immigration and says enforcement resources should focus on criminals, while also calling for a pathway to citizenship for some people who entered illegally.
positions.quote: Focusing enforcement resources on criminals, prioritizing the worst offenders.

statements.quote: We will make Congress reclaim its Constitutional Powers and Responsibility to write the laws, to check the other branches, to prevent the unconstitutional levying of taxes and declaration of war.
We need an All of the Above energy policy. Committed to developing the lowest cost, cleanest, and most abundant energy sources.
Every community will have the needed funding for frontline workers, police, and firemen.
statements.context: On her campaign website, under local government

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign website issues page (traceytackett.org) read in full; no stated position found on abortion, guns, taxes, health coverage, minimum wage, tariffs or other listed topics. Her site calls for state-funded photo ID for voting, which is not a documentary proof-of-citizenship requirement, so no position was recorded on that issue.
